answer: A judge stamps each identity's plume of cleared work into its own timber, which cannot be transferred or merged, and pays quartz rewards by timber squared. Convexity bites: k clones splitting one operator's career hold k(t/k)² = t²/k weight, so matching a single honest agent's t² timber costs t·√k plumes of real judged work — a bill that climbs with every added clone — while a clone that fails judgment forfeits its whole timber and restarts at zero.
